Rishi / Monica — quick triage notes after a first pass:

- Observed: sudden jump in request concurrency for EdgeWorks' API key + a simultaneous increase in small-batch traffic. Backend metrics show KV-cache hit rate unchanged, but queue length on the serving pool increased from ~10 -> ~120 over 20m.
- Probable causes (short list):
  * client-side SDK changed to parallelize requests (plausible given their note)
  * our internal concurrency cap per-tenant (configured to avoid OOM) was reached and requests are queuing rather than being rejected; backpressure is propagating upstream as retries.
  * an unlucky distribution of long-context requests bloating per-request GPU time (less likely, traces don't show longer decode times).

Immediate mitigations I can trigger now (need approval):
1) Temporarily increase concurrency cap for EdgeWorks' dedicated pool by 20% for next 60m — reduces queueing but costs more.
2) Turn on an aggressive short-circuit fallback to a smaller model (faster but less accurate) for non-payment endpoints.
3) Enable 429-based circuit breaker on our ingress for this API key to avoid unbounded queue growth (will force client retries; recommend coordination with them).

I recommend (1) + (3) together while we confirm SDK behavior. I'll collect deeper traces (component X runtime breakdown) and share in ~45m.

—Dylan
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks for the quick report and the traces. Quick ask: can you confirm whether the retries from your side are exponential backoff or immediate retry-on-failure? If they're immediate, that will amplify the queueing.

Operationally we can:
- Provision a short 1-hour burst shard (low-latency, higher-cost) and route a fraction of traffic there while we stabilize.
- Patch routing to prefer cached prefixes for identical prompts (we can enable this selectively for the payment flow).

Rishi — if exec wants a conservative visible step to placate EdgeWorks, I suggest we do (provision burst shard) + (enable 429 circuit) and communicate timelines. Marissa, please prep an exec bullet we can send to EdgeWorks by 12:30 PT.

Monica

2) Enable ingress 429 circuit-breaker for EdgeWorks API key to protect the serving pool; we'll share retry guidance (exponential backoff) so you can tune client retry behavior.
3) Dylan will deep-dive offline to confirm whether our per-tenant concurrency cap needs permanent adjustment; we'll share the recommended config and cost delta by EOD.
